A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniMotion and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. Content can be matched reliably despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original seven-task evaluations, architectural ablations, reconstruction analyses, and zero-shot 3DPW results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports a frozen-backbone-only Vision-to-Motion comparison.

M1.justification: The CMA-VAE, DPA, LRA, dual-path embedders, hybrid attention, routed LoRA, and generation procedures remain unchanged. The revised architecture illustration and added explanations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both retain the same seven tasks and HumanML3D/AMASS, MotionFix, Human3.6M, MoVid, and 3DPW coverage. The zero-shot 3DPW evaluation highlighted in v2 already appears in v1 Appendix C.3.

E2.justification: Section 4.2 adds a frozen pose-aware-backbone-only comparator, reporting 86.9 MPJPE against UniMotion's 75.0. Existing comparator membership in Tables 2–14 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported Vision-to-Motion evaluation gains a backbone-only control. Existing splits, metrics, training budgets, and inference settings remain unchanged; the single-reference-image protocol emphasized in v2 was already documented in v1 Appendix E.

E4.justification: The new backbone-only comparison provides a limited check of whether performance derives merely from pretrained visual features. Existing DPA/LRA and architecture ablations, reconstruction analyses, shuffled-condition testing, and 3DPW generalization analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E.3 retains averaging Text-to-Motion metrics over 20 runs with different random seeds. Neither version adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or changed uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports 86.9 MPJPE for the frozen backbone alone in Section 4.2. Existing performance tables and plots are unchanged, including UniMotion's 75.0 Human3.6M MPJPE and 93.6 zero-shot 3DPW MPJPE.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, attention-mask definition, and Appendix C reasoning remain unchanged. Several displayed equations become inline expressions, producing renumbering without changing their mathematics.

C1.justification: Both retain the same claimed seven-task Motion–Text–RGB unification and continuous-representation, DPA, and LRA contributions. The added explanation about integrating motion into a pretrained Text–RGB backbone restates the existing contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly attributes performance mainly to DPA/LRA rather than the frozen backbone. The conclusion explicitly limits evaluated coverage to single-person motion and describes multi-person interaction as compatible with the attention design but left for future work.

D1.justification: Table 1 adds backbone parameter counts, including 220M for MotionGPT and MG-MotionLLM and 7B for HMVLM. These are additional disclosures, not evidence of resized experimental models. The detailed implementation and training recipe in Appendices D–E remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on VLM personalization and parallel diffusion decoding, removes Brown et al., UST-SSM, and robotic-view action-recognition references, and replaces the quantization citation with VQ-VAE. Its overall research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized explanatory additions and wording edits, expanded affiliations, a new acknowledgement, and removal of several appendix signposts. The main narrative organization and Appendices A–F remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with branch labels and a legend; Figures 3 and 4 are enlarged from text-wrapped placements. Table 1 gains a Size column, and page formatting and display placement change. The other figure contents are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves readability through clearer architectural displays and makes model sizes and single-person evaluation limits more explicit. The backbone-only comparison adds limited supporting evidence, although its configuration remains sparsely described. These are useful refinements; the method and existing benchmark evidence remain essentially unchanged.
